newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - firms up, but trading light.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - firms up, but trading light.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices firmed again, with long-dollar bonds quoted 1/8 to a 1/4 of a point higher, but secondary activity was light, and a few traders speculated the market's rise might slow or stall.
"Municipals are hard-pressed in here, because of the levels we're at," a trader said, citing their recent strong performance vis a vis the Treasury market.
Another trader said the firming tone only amounted to about a gain of 0.01. "It continues to kind of grind higher, but there's not really any noticeable appreciation," he said.

One of the most closely watched deals scheduled for Thursday, a $356 million sale of refunding bonds by the Municipal Assistance Corp (MAC) for New York City, was priced at 4.95 percent in 2008 by Goldman Sachs & Co.
MAC deals typically draw fairly strong demand due to the prominence of the issuer and its creditworthiness, and the offering was the largest on the negotiated calender.
Municipal bond sales for Thursday were expected to total $1.3 billion in 35 sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.
On the competitive side, 12 sales totaling $136 million are scheduled. A $23 million Warren County, Ky., deal at 1100 EDT was the largest.

While the municipal market has been anticipating big buys by fund managers due to a huge wave of redemptions in June and July, at least one trader was skeptical about how much new cash might be available.
"I think most of it's spent," he said. Later, he added: "I think they've been spending it the last few months in anticipation, but how much is really there, I don't know."
An important yardstick of the secondary market, the Standard and Poor's Corp Blue List, stood at $1.4 billion, up from leaner levels seen a few weeks ago.

In early trade, fixed-income markets got a bit of a helping hand from a slightly surprising weekly unemployment report, which showed initial claims rose to 347,000. Economists polled by Reuters had predicted the claims for the week of June 14 to add up to 333,000.

The trade data also contained a few surprises, as the U.S. international trade defict was pegged at $8.36 billion in April. That was well below forecasts for a $10 billion gap, even though it marked a 7.8 percent increase from March's figure, which was revised down.
The latest data showed the economy had not cooled quite as much as many economists had expected from the frothy 5.8 percent annual rate of growth seen in the first quarter.
September municipal futures firmed four ticks to 118-14/32, a rise matched by September Treasury futures, which stood at 112-9/32. The MOB spread between the two contracts remained at 197 ticks.
In secondary trading, Orange County, Florida, School Board Certificates of Participation, of 2022, which pay a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were bid at 5.55 percent, NET, up one basis point.
And Delaware River Port Authority of Pennsylvania and New Jersey of 2026, which carry a 5-1/2 percent coupon, were bid at 99-5/8, up two-eighths.
